Sample.evidence_source: Five women and eight men, aged 22–53, were included in the shame analysis.

Population.evidence_source: Five women and eight men, aged 22–53, were included in the shame analysis. Five were first time suicide attempters; three respondents had made one attempt previously; three respondents had made two attempts and the remaining two respondents had made three or more suicide attempts previously.

Type.evidence_source: All respondents were diagnosed by an experienced psychiatrist, as part of the clinical investigation.

Area.evidence_source: Five were first time suicide attempters; three respondents had made one attempt previously; three respondents had made two attempts and the remaining two respondents had made three or more suicide attempts previously. Seven of the respondents had attempted suicide by drug overdose; two had deep cuts along the forearm, two had tried to suffocate themselves with carbon monoxide, one had jumped from a height and one respondent had tried four different suicide methods during a period of 1 day (overdose, wrist slitting, drowning, and hanging). The respondents' scores for suicide intent, as measured by the Suicide Intent Scale (SIS) (20), ranged from 11 to 25 (mean 17, SD 5). According to the classification by Strosahl et al. (21), the mean score of suicide intent expressed by the respondents was moderate. Twelve of the respondents were diagnosed as meeting the criteria for one or more Axis-1 disorder (major depression n ¼ 11, alcohol dependence n ¼ 3, anxiety disorders n ¼ 4, adjustment disorder n ¼ 1) on the DSM-III-R diagnostic system (22). Seven respondents also met the criteria for one or two personality disorders (personality disorder UNS n ¼ 2, borderline n ¼ 2, dependent n ¼ 2, masochistic n ¼ 1, antisocial n ¼ 1).
